title: The Crimson Swine Dies Twice
text: “Let's see it, then…”
And so the merchants started muttering amongst themselves yet again, I say.
“We don't exactly have all day, you know?”
I wanted to ask about the Crimson Swine's whereabouts, but this mysterious back-and-forth of negotiation and authentication was nothing but a waste of time, indeed.
“This is… probably genuine.”
“Don't be ridiculous! The only ones who could pull something like this off would be the Legendary Heroes—”
Right as he said that, a merchant I recognized placed a hand on the shoulder of one of the Assassin's Guild staff.
“Guh…”
“That's not very becoming of someone from this establishment, I'd say.”
“If someone brings something like this into a place like this, of course we're gonna react this way, no matter how composed we usually are! This isn't the Merchant's Guild!”
It seemed they'd more or less grasped the situation now, because they settled down after that.
“So? Just how much is it worth? If you're lying to me… well, I wonder what I'd have to do about that.”

Ah… it really is hard to talk this way. I wanted to tack on an "indeed" to that too, I say. In my head, Father was making some sort of exasperated face. You really want to keep up that speech pattern that badly? he seemed to be thinking. Ha ha ha! I've been talking like this for so long now that it's just second nature, I say.
“We're talking sums on the scale of a national budget, literally. We're looking forward to the next auction—this isn't something you just casually hand over in a place like this.”

For a moment, in the back of my mind, I pictured Father and the others—all the ones who'd worked so hard as merchants—lined up together wearing that sort of shadowed, twilight expression people get when something dawns on them.
『I… if I'd just taken that thing to the right place, I wouldn't have had to grind away earning money bit by bit…』

I feel like that's what they were saying, but surely it's just my imagination, I say. The world isn't soft enough that some gold trinket with no special properties whatsoever would fetch that kind of money, indeed. These guys were just making a big fuss over nothing, I'm sure.

“Hoh… well, in that case, dispose of it however you like. In exchange, just make sure you treat me well here. Don't you dare leak any information to anyone asking about me. If you do, I won't hold back, and I'll come take back whatever profit you made off that thing, understand? It's business.”
I issued my demands, mimicking Father's manner. Let's call it killing two birds with one stone—getting the Crimson Swine's location while also sealing these people's mouths at the same time.
The assembled group there whispered amongst themselves for a while, but eventually they nodded, accepting my terms.
“Understood. This was about information regarding the Melromarc princess, correct?”
And with that, I managed to pin down the Crimson Swine's general location, I say.
“She's currently traveling slowly with members of the Three Heroes Church of Melromarc.”

Nothing particularly strange about that, it seemed. Still, this was a chance, I say—a chance to seize her location. It seemed the Assassin's Guild folks, thrilled over such a valuable item, were going to restrict the flow of information, making it harder for anyone to trace me. I managed to get more detailed information out of them. Now all that was left was where to finish off the Crimson Swine, I say. Sneaking into an inn and erasing her in the dark of night sounded good, didn't it? That would be easy enough, indeed. Either way, speed was of the essence.
“My thanks. See you.”
“Oi. That's it? That's all you want?”
“It's a pain. Do whatever you like with it.”

Dealing with these people seriously seemed like more trouble than it was worth. I'll come back if I ever need anything else! And with that, I concluded the transaction, left the information broker's guild, and made my way straight toward the Crimson Swine's location, I say.
In any case, I'd managed to track her movements, I say.
“That carriage there, I'd say.”

Along the road from Faubrey to Melromarc, right in the middle of a mountain pass, the Crimson Swine and her lot appeared to be making their way through. Members of the Three Heroes Church, along with Melromarc knights, were accompanying them. Since the Crimson Swine was technically Melromarc royalty, of course she'd have an escort at a time like this.

It made for a fine marker, I say. What's more, trailing behind the carriage was a whole procession hauling along all sorts of goods, clothing included, like some sort of caravan. According to the information broker's guild, these were things the Crimson Swine had purchased—piled up goods not meant for any trade or commerce. Come to think of it, back in the first loop, when I was still a fool, I recall seeing similar items in the castle's wardrobe room. Where does she even get that kind of money? Well, probably some kind of support from Trash, I'd wager. Likely charged it all to Melromarc's account or something.

By the way, after the Queen returned, all those items in the wardrobe room basically vanished. Surely sold off. Now then, striking her down swiftly was for the best going forward. I'd considered waiting until she checked into some inn in some town or country and finishing her off in her room, but that would eat up the whole day.

Ha ha ha, time is money, indeed. And this mountain pass was exactly the sort of place where bandits showing up wouldn't be the least bit strange, so I figured I'd just wipe them all out in one go! I took position on a slightly elevated spot a short distance away, readied my spear, and prepared to throw. Something seemed to whisper that I ought to take her alive instead, but I had no time for that, I say.
“Aiming Lancer IV!”
Fwoosh! The spear I hurled came raining down right toward the Crimson Swine and the knights, I say.
“GYAAAAAAAAAAAAAAH!?”
“W-who goes there!?”
“Just what bandit is this!?”
“What is this!? This rain!?”
“BUHYAAAAAAAAAAAAAAH!?”

Screams of agony rang out amid the pile of bodies, but I paid them no mind, indeed. More importantly, if I didn't make this look like bandit work, the whole disguise would be pointless. So I figured I'd just keep the momentum going and blast them with something like Drifa Firestorm V, but since I wanted another spell with that same "raining down" restriction as Aiming Lancer, I went with Drifa Fire Rain V instead, raining down fire. Doh-doh-doh! The rain of flame came pouring down toward the carriage where the Crimson Swine was riding.
“Buhyaaaaaaaaaaaaah!?”
A pig that looked like it had to be the Crimson Swine tried desperately to flee the carriage, though honestly, I couldn't tell one pig from another, I say.
“P-Princess Malty! P-please, hurry—”

Oh? Good, that confirms it's the Crimson Swine! My thanks to that knight, I say. Drop dead, I say! And with that, I closed the distance with Cloaking Lance and ran the Crimson Swine straight through, I say.
“Bu— BUHYAAAA!”
Ohh, this liveliness—or rather, this sheer resilience—was unmistakably the Crimson Swine. So I finished her off with Burst Lance, I say.
“Drop dead, I say! Burst Lance X!”
“BUHYAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAH!?”
A clean, successful detonation of the Crimson Swine, I say.
Well… I guess that's fine? That's fine, isn't it? I think that's about right, you know.

In my head, the spirit of the spear, Rival, and Rabbit Guy were each sending me these pointed looks while affirming what I'd done. Motoyasu, didn't you mess up how you handled the Crimson Swine somewhere along the way? Another me inside my head seemed to whisper that, but I couldn't quite make sense of it, indeed. No! This is exactly right! I thought. In case her soul needed disposing of too, lest something strange happen, I followed up with a weapon specialized against souls just to be safe, I say.
『Buh… buhyaaa—』
Fuhaha! The Crimson Swine dies twice, I say. Ka-boom! A flashy impact erupted. Even in a state where I couldn't sense souls, that death cry was enough to make me feel something, indeed.
“This confirms it without a doubt, I say!”
Mm-hmm. Yeah, sure. That's probably right, isn't it? That's fine, I guess.
Never mind Father, but the other two need to shut it, I say! I wasn't wrong, I say! This was the correct call, indeed!
“Princess Malty!? You bastard! Do you have any idea what you've done!? The nation won't stand for this!”
One of the fallen knights was muttering something, but I had no intention of letting him escape, I say.
“Of course I know, don't I? And I won't let any of you get away either, I say.”

The Crimson Swine was simply going to vanish without a trace along with her escort, on a mountain road on her way back to the nation! I'd want to make this look as much like bandit work as possible—preferably not anything pointing to demi-humans or beastmen, if I could help it.
“What!? D-don't tell me you… do you even know what we're transporting—”
Hm? Were they hauling something alongside the Crimson Swine?
“Either way, the lot of you are going to disappear, I say!”
“Wha—!? GYAAAAAAAAAAAH!?”

And with that, I wiped out the rest of the Crimson Swine's entourage. Since it needed to look like part of the cargo had been stolen, I made sure to burn the clothing and such among the shipment until not even ashes remained. All sorts of debris lay scattered about the area. Among it, there rolled a crate that the knights seemed to have been guarding with particular care. Judging by the sheer number of escorts, it almost looked like they'd been prioritizing this over the Crimson Swine herself. Just what were they transporting?

So I pried open the box—plain-looking on the outside, but locked down with considerable rigor. There seemed to be some sort of magical mechanism rigged to it, but I smashed the whole thing apart regardless, I say! Something like a curse came bursting out, but it had no effect on me, indeed. I cleaved straight through the curse along with the box using my spear. And what came out from inside was… something that looked like a metal plate. What's this, I wondered? But… I'd seen this before, somewhere. Searching through my memory, its shape matched the ceremonial tools used in Hero Summonings.
